ministry_ne: संस्कृति पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्यन मन्त्रालय
summary:
The main purpose of the Nepal Civil Aviation Authority Bill, 2083 is to amend and consolidate the laws relating to the Civil Aviation Authority to develop and expand Nepal's civil aviation service in accordance with international standards, prevent unlawful interference, and make civil aviation service safe, regular, standard, reliable, and accessible through effective regulation (Preamble, Page 19). This Act shall come into force on the ninety-first day from the date of authentication (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 19).

The service provider organizations covered under this Bill include air service operators, air navigation service providers, aerodrome, helipad, and heliport operators, aircraft and aircraft part manufacturing or maintenance organizations, aviation training institutions, ground handling service providers, air service agents, flight clearance agents, and recreational aviation operators (Section 2, Clause w, Page 21). Anyone wishing to commercially operate air services in Nepal must obtain an air operator certificate from the Authority, foreign air services wishing to operate commercial flights in Nepal must obtain a foreign air operator certificate, and these certificates must be renewed (Section 12, Subsections 1, 2 and 3, Page 28). Anyone wishing to operate aircraft manufacturing, maintenance, sale of aircraft or parts, ground handling service, approved aviation training, air service agency, flight clearance agency, or recreational aviation activities must obtain an aviation business operation certificate from the Authority (Section 13, Subsection 1, Pages 28-29). Anyone wishing to operate an aerodrome in Nepal must obtain registration and an aerodrome operation certificate in accordance with standards and conditions set by the Authority and renew it, though designated domestic aerodromes may operate services with only a registration certificate (Section 30, Subsections 1 and 3, Page 33). Anyone wishing to provide air navigation services in Nepal must obtain an air navigation service provider certificate from the Authority and renew it as prescribed (Section 32, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 34). Anyone wishing to operate unmanned aircraft in Nepal's airspace must obtain a permit from the Authority (Section 19, Subsection 2, Page 31). Aircraft flying in Nepal must carry on board the registration certificate, certificate of airworthiness, individual licenses or certificates of crew members, logbook, radio station license, passenger details, cargo details, dangerous goods details, manuals, and other prescribed documents (Section 16, Pages 29-30). Service provider organizations must mandatorily insure aircraft according to prevailing law or as determined by the Authority before flying in Nepal's airspace, and must immediately inform the Authority of any accident, risk, or violation related to flight safety and aviation security (Section 50, Clauses a and b, Page 45). Permanent employees working in the former Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal who wish to remain in the Authority must submit an application to the Ministry through the Authority within sixty days from the date specified by the Nepal Government by publishing a notice in the Nepal Gazette (Section 43, Subsection 1, Page 40).

The Authority issues, renews, restricts, suspends, or cancels certificates or licenses for air service operation, airworthiness, recreational aviation, air navigation, aerodrome, helipad, and heliport operation, aviation training institutions, aircraft and part manufacturing or maintenance or overhaul, import, export, sale, commercial flights of foreign air services, ground handling, and agency businesses (Section 5, Clause a, Subclause 1, Page 22). The Authority issues type certificates or grants recognition to type certificates for aircraft, engines, or propellers (Section 5, Clause a, Subclause 2, Page 23; Section 25, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 32). The Director General shall issue individual licenses for up to a maximum period of five years to personnel required for functions such as flight operations, maintenance, flight dispatching, and air traffic control, and may grant recognition to licenses issued by member states of the International Civil Aviation Organization (Section 34, Subsections 1, 2 and 3, Pages 34-35). To fly in Nepal's airspace, an aircraft must obtain a certificate of airworthiness in the prescribed format from the Authority, and an aircraft without a certificate or with an expired certificate shall not fly (Section 26, Subsections 1, 2 and 3, Page 32). Before flying, aircraft operators must have all machinery and equipment tested by an authorized technician and certified as airworthy (Section 28, Page 33). Aircraft maintenance must be conducted by an authorized organization as specified in the certificate of airworthiness (Section 29, Page 33). Unregistered aircraft shall not fly in Nepal, double registration is prohibited, but aircraft deregistered in another country may be registered in Nepal subject to this Act (Section 20, Page 31; Section 21, Subsection 3, Page 31). The Authority sets standards and regulates air navigation services, meteorological services, firefighting, passenger services, equipment installation, signals, noise and gas emissions, dangerous goods transport, and security oversight (Section 5, Clause c, Pages 23-24). The Director General shall designate inspectors based on qualifications and experience to inspect and regulate compliance with flight safety and aviation security standards (Section 44, Subsections 1 and 2, Pages 40-41). Inspectors may conduct covert tests with prior approval of the Director General, and a separate Quality Assurance Unit may be formed under the Director General to test the quality of inspection work (Section 44, Subsections 7 and 11, Pages 41-42).
